meta.name: Build a rising-topic reading shortlist from RSS feeds to HTML and CSV

name: Find rising RSS topics and build a balanced reading shortlist

parameters.content:
## Find rising RSS topics and build a balanced reading shortlist

### Who is it for?
For editors, researchers or anyone who follows the same subjects across several news feeds and wants a useful place to start reading.

### What it does
Reads four public RSS or Atom feeds, removes unwanted entries, assigns topics and groups similar headlines. It compares the last 12 hours with the previous 36 hours to spot changes in coverage.

The added shortlist picks up to five fresh stories. Stories covered by multiple publishers come first, with at most two picks per topic. Each pick includes source links and a short reason. This keeps one busy subject from filling the whole list.

### Setup
Open Configure Feed Sources (Edit Fields) and edit the JSON fields for feeds and keywords. Run the whole workflow manually. In each Download node, open Output → Binary → data and download the file. Review feed health before using the results.

### Requirements
An n8n version with a four-input Merge node and internet access to the feeds. No credentials, API services or extra packages.

### Customization
Change the keywords, time windows, shortlist size and limit per topic in Configure Feed Sources. Adjust the weekday schedule if needed. The workflow does not retain history or verify news; feed coverage may be incomplete.

## Start and configure

Edit feed URLs, topic keywords and limits in Configure Feed Sources. Then run the whole workflow manually.

Weekday schedule runs at 08:00 and 20:00 UTC, Monday to Friday, after activation. Change the times and timezone before using it.

## Read and merge feeds

Read four public RSS/Atom feeds and wait for all four before processing. No credentials needed.

Empty or failed feeds remain visible in the report. Use the same publisher ID for feeds from one outlet.

## Filter and tag articles

Remove old, undated, excluded and duplicate entries. Assign each article to its strongest keyword match. Titles count more than summaries; topic order breaks ties.

## Analyze topic momentum

Group similar headlines and compare the latest 12 hours with the preceding 36 hours.

Rising and Surging need multiple stories and publishers. Limited means incomplete coverage. No history is stored between runs.

## Select and build brief

Pick up to 5 fresh stories, with at most 2 per topic. Groups covered by multiple publishers come first, then topic momentum, publisher count and recency.

Change shortlistSize and maxShortlistPerTopic in Configure Feed Sources. Each pick has links and a reason. Coverage does not verify the story.

## Download files

Open either output node: Output → Binary → data → Download.

HTML: shortlist, links, topic table and feed health.

CSV: all topic metrics and shortlisted story counts.

Empty results still produce both files. Files stay in execution data according to your retention settings.
